audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the level chart hands Swain 4 of 7 stages and Tahm Kench 0, while Tahm Kench wins this lane 57.06% over 680 games. The chart says the opposite of the result.
audit.why: Swain genuinely owns levels 3-5 — Nevermove plus Vision of Empire is a real poke pattern against a melee with no dash. But level 6 and first item are where the matchup turns: Devour suppresses Swain out of his own Demonic Ascension, and he has no dash, blink or escape to break a three-stack setup. Those two stages belong to Tahm Kench, which is where the 57% comes from.
audit.corrected: Levels 3 and 4-5 stay Swain; Level 6 and First item flip to Tahm Kench; Level 1, Level 2 and 2+ items stay Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] tells you to dodge Nevermove by "hugging a minion wave to break the snare geometry". Nevermove's outgoing wave does not root — only the wave returning to Swain applies the 1.5s root.
audit.why: The dodge is a direction problem, not a minion problem. A player who hugs the wave and then walks straight back toward his side of the lane walks along the return line and eats the root anyway.
audit.corrected: Only the returning half of Nevermove roots (1.5s). Once the wave has flown past you, step sideways off its return path rather than retreating down it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls Tahm Kench's W "Abyssal Voyage" and uses it as a disengage ("use Abyssal Voyage to disengage or Flash away"). Tahm Kench's W is Abyssal Dive and he has no global or disengage ability.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive is a 1.35s channel into a short blink and knockup, on a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown. Told to disengage with it against a Swain who has just ulted, a player channels for 1.35 seconds inside the drain and takes the whole thing.
audit.corrected: Swain popping Demonic Ascension is the cue to commit Devour, not to disengage — you have no disengage. Abyssal Dive is an engage knockup you spend after his root is gone.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Abyssal Dive

audit.whatIsWrong: The text says "play around his E cooldown" without ever giving the number, and points all the cooldown tracking at Demonic Ascension instead.
audit.why: Nevermove is the ability that actually gates your walk-up, at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s. Demonic Ascension is 120s and is a reason to commit, not to wait. Naming the real number turns 'bait his E' into a countable window.
audit.corrected: Track Nevermove (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) as the walk-up gate; Vision of Empire takes a full 1.5s to detonate, so its circle is walkable rather than tankable.
sources: League Wiki — Swain: Nevermove, Vision of Empire

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.mid tells you to give nothing while Demonic Ascension is up, which inverts the win condition.
audit.why: Devour is a suppression that removes Swain from his own drain and he has no mobility to answer it. Refusing to fight while his ultimate is available hands him free sustained damage in every skirmish; the correct rule is to bait the root, then commit into the ultimate.
audit.corrected: Trade around Nevermove's cooldown; treat Demonic Ascension coming on as the Devour cue.
sources: League Wiki — Tahm Kench: Devour (suppression, requires 3 An Acquired Taste stacks)

audit.why: Mercury's Treads, Spirit Visage and an early anti-heal component are the right call against Ravenous Flock's 6%-max-health-per-fragment healing and the Demonic Ascension drain.
The packet flagged "Stack An Acquired Taste" in wants.you[0] as a probable wrong ability name. It is a false positive — An Acquired Taste is the correct passive name and the sentence is fine.

edits.before: Swain's E (Nevermove) roots you in place at range — dodge it by hugging a minion wave to break the snare geometry, or he freely combos W+Q on you without risk.
edits.after: Swain's E (Nevermove) only roots on the way BACK — the outgoing wave is harmless, so step off its return line instead of retreating straight down it.

edits.before: Once Swain has E+W+Q online he can pull-root-bomb from distance and chunk you badly; respect his range until you can bait his E cooldown before engaging.
edits.after: With E+W+Q online he can root-then-bomb, but Vision of Empire needs 1.5s to detonate — walk out of the circle instead of tanking it, and bait Nevermove first.

edits.before: Land E (Nevermove) to root you in place and freely chain W bomb and Q poke without counterplay
edits.after: Land the returning half of Nevermove — the outgoing wave is harmless, so he fires past you and waits

edits.before: Swain sharpens his edge from levels 4-6: his E cooldown is short enough that he can threaten a pull every wave, and once he hits 6 his R drain means any extended trade in his range is a losing proposition for you — he heals back through your autos while soul stacks compound. Play around his E cooldown as the key timing: when Nevermove is down you can step up, fish for stacks with Tongue Lash, and threaten the 3-stack stun, but the moment his E is back up you retreat. Respect the ult — if he pops R do NOT let him sit on you; use Abyssal Voyage to disengage or Flash away rather than trading into the drain.
edits.after: Swain sharpens his edge from levels 4-6: Nevermove is only 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, so he can threaten a root every wave, and his soul stacks compound off every fragment he collects. Play around that root as the key timing — remember only the RETURNING wave roots, so once it has flown past you step sideways rather than retreating down its line. When it is down you step up, fish for stacks with Tongue Lash, and threaten the 3-stack stun. Vision of Empire takes a full 1.5 seconds to detonate, so its circle is something you walk out of, not something you tank. Once you have Devour, him popping Demonic Ascension is your cue to commit, not to run.

edits.before: Your first item is the turning point where this lane finally tilts back. Heartsteel or Sunfire means your grey-health healing starts outpacing his drain poke, and the Devour combo at 3 stacks can pull him out of his own R, completely shutting off the soul-drain engine he needs to win trades. From here, bait his E before every engage — if Nevermove is on cooldown and you have 3 stacks, that is a kill window; if his E is up, back off. At 2+ items the matchup returns to genuine skill expression: your near-unkillable tankiness and point-and-click lockdown against his sustained AOE drain and soul stacks; neither side wins cleanly, but team-fight disruption through Devour and Abyssal Voyage is where you make the matchup irrelevant.
edits.after: Your first item is the turning point where this lane finally tilts back. Heartsteel or Sunfire means your grey-health healing starts outpacing his drain poke, and the Devour combo at 3 stacks suppresses him out of his own R, completely shutting off the soul-drain engine he needs to win trades. From here, bait his E before every engage — if Nevermove is on cooldown and you have 3 stacks, that is a kill window; if his E is up, back off. At 2+ items the matchup returns to genuine skill expression: Thick Skin banks 42-50% of incoming damage as grey health once two or more enemies are on you, so team-fight disruption through Devour and a timed Abyssal Dive knockup is where you make the matchup irrelevant.

edits.before: Swain's R makes any extended engagement his — soul-drain heals back through your autos while AOE stacks build; respect the ult timer and disengage with Abyssal Voyage rather than trading into it.
edits.after: Devour answers Demonic Ascension directly: three stacks plus the 1.5s Tongue Lash stun let you suppress him out of his own drain, and Swain has no dash or blink to break the setup once you are on him.

edits.before: His R drain plus first-item AP means he out-sustains you through the spike window; deny him roam kills by staying in lane and stacking Heartsteel passively until YOUR first item flips the attrition war.
edits.after: Heartsteel plus Thick Skin banking 15-47% of what he chips you for outpaces his drain poke; Nevermove is the only thing keeping you off him, so bait the 10-12s root and walk straight in.

edits.before: Build MR — Q-stun him, dodge his E root. Tahm Kench wins the Demonic Ascension cooldown windows.
edits.after: Build MR — sustain his poke, then Devour him straight out of his own Demonic Ascension drain.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Trade when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s): only the returning wave roots, and it is the one thing gating your walk-up — bait it, then step. - Demonic Ascension (120s) is your Devour cue, not a retreat cue.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Demonic Ascension: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade around Nevermove, not his ult: when the root is down you get a free walk-up. If he pops Demonic Ascension, that is your Devour window, not a retreat.

edits.before: Devour deletes him from the fight — or you from his. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Swain's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Devour suppresses him out of Demonic Ascension. He has no dash — three stacks and a stun is a full kill window at 6.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. Trade when it’s down. When it is down — Q-AA + R him.
edits.after: Nevermove roots only on the return, 1.5s. Devour suppresses Swain out of Demonic Ascension — stun, eat.
